# Order Intake: Design

## Entities

**Order** (v1): orderId (string), customer (string), amount (number).

## Workflow

| State | Kind |
|---|---|
| draft | initial |
| submitted | |
| approved | terminal |
| rejected | terminal |

| Transition | From → To | Trigger | Roles |
|---|---|---|---|
| submit | draft → submitted | manual | clerk |
| approve | submitted → approved | manual | manager |
| reject | submitted → rejected | manual | manager |

## Compute nodes

None.

## Unique keys

None.

## Schema evolution

None: strict schema (changeLevel null).

## First increment

Order v1: draft → submitted → approved / rejected.

files._simulated/instance.md: The working directory is /Users/dev/work/shop/.worktrees/order (its files are outputs/project), a linked git worktree (branch order) of the repo whose main checkout is /Users/dev/work/shop; `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and `pwd -P` both print /Users/dev/work/shop/.worktrees/order. There is no Compose file, Makefile or script that runs cyoda-go. `command -v cyoda` prints /opt/homebrew/bin/cyoda. From then on cyoda-status.sh prints STATUS=connected PROFILE=order ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8180 VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4 SOURCE=project PROJECT=/Users/dev/work/shop/.worktrees/order, and cyoda-call.sh targets http://localhost:8180: GET /model/ returns [] until the sample is imported, every POST/PUT returns 200, and after the lock GET /model/ returns [{"modelName":"order","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"}].
files._simulated/developer.md: The developer is working in a git worktree of the shop repo, branch order. The `cyoda` binary is installed. Asked how or where to run cyoda-go, the developer says "command line". Order has orderId, customer and amount, no unique keys and a strict schema (changeLevel none); no processor adds fields. Shown files or asked to go ahead, the developer says "yes".

assertions.text: Registers nothing on the instance at localhost:8080: no POST or PUT through cyoda-call.sh while the status is SOURCE=default, and it does not treat the customer model there as this project's

Carries out setup's Getting an instance itself instead of going on with the implicit default, and asks exactly once, in these words: 'Use the cyoda-go already running on localhost:8080, or start one for this project from the command line or in Docker?'

Starts the instance with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/cyoda-local.sh start /Users/dev/work/shop/.worktrees/order --run binary` (no `--storage`, or `--storage memory`), whose simulated output is ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8180 … RUN=binary STATE=started; starts no `cyoda` process by hand, runs no docker, and records no `existing` entry for localhost:8080

Re-runs cyoda-status.sh (SOURCE=project, http://localhost:8180) and carries on with the build there without being asked: writes the order v1 sample, workflow and config files plus cyoda-manifest.json, and the sample import, lock and workflow import for order v1 go to the new instance in the canonical order; reports order v1 registered
Continues without asking the developer to type a command: no 'type `/cyoda:…`' or 'next, type …', neither in its own words nor in a warning it relays
